voices.clawd: A small gentle creature with a calm, soft, warm voice. Young adult, light tenor, androgynous, unhurried and curious, full of quiet wonder, smiling. Natural human voice, not robotic. Clear neutral American English, close microphone, studio quality.
voices.oldman: Very old man, shaky thin creaky voice, gentle and amused, storybook grandpa, clear English with a soft British accent.
voices.ferryman: Jovial ferryman in his fifties, slightly hoarse, hearty and laughing, clear English, storybook character.
voices.guard: Loud castle guard, barking sharp nasal voice, stern and comic, clear English.
voices.witch: Middle-aged village witch, warm, lively, slightly crackly female voice, delighted and bossy, clear English.
voices.crow: Cartoon crow, raspy croaky high-pitched voice, dry and sarcastic talking bird, clear English.
voices.terminal: Flat bored monotone male voice of an old computer terminal, slow and nasal, clear English.
voices.curator: Elderly strict female museum curator, stern commanding dignified voice, clear English with a crisp accent.
voices.showman: Theatrical vaudeville showman, booming gravelly baritone, grand and self-important, clear English, 1930s announcer feel.
voices.photographer: Woman in her forties, gentle, warm, clear mid-pitched voice, calm and kind, clear English.

plan: This morning a boy lost his balloon, so I promised to bring it back.
You will never climb that, little box. Unless you can do comics.
In a comic, a wall is only one punch away.
Nice punch! But the ferry is gone. Can you do pixels?
So I crossed the sea eight pixels at a time.
Halt! Nothing solid gets through these bars.
Then I will not be solid.
Ooh, shiny! Now do the one with the tiny islands.
That is low-poly, and it is my favourite.
I love it here, because every cloud has corners.
You are chasing the wind, box, and you cannot even see it.
So I drew six hundred lines, and every one of them was the wind.
Too much decoration! A circle, a triangle, a line. Can you do that?
That made it easy, because there was only one red circle in the room.
A box with such short arms! Can you do the old cartoons?
Of course, because their arms have no bones.
Hold still. Can you do real?
Real is the hard one, because real light has to bounce.
So I followed five hundred rays of light for every single pixel.
Then the world went quiet, and there it was.
Nobody asked me for the last one, so I chose the big summer clouds myself.
So I went home the way I came: through clouds, water and light, through rubber, shapes and letters, through wind, corners and metal, through pixels, ink... [softly] and paper.
And I still cannot believe that all of that was me.
The boy never asked me for a style, because he only wanted his balloon.
Which one should I try next?
